text: 10-month-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. The mother notes that the wheezing exacerbates when the child is crying, feeding, and when his neck is flexed. Additionally, there are instances where the child vomits after feeding.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details; the worsening of symptoms with neck flexion and vomiting is very specific. Given the age and the nature of these episodes, could you tell me if the stridor is louder when he is lying on his back or if it improves when he stands or sits up?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. I also have Exacerbation during crying, Exacerbation during feeding, Exacerbation with neck flexion, Relief with neck extension, Occasional vomiting post-feeding.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Laryngomalacia with associated gastroesophageal reflux.

Based on the classic triad of inspiratory stridor worsening with crying, feeding, and neck flexion, along with post-feeding vomiting, the clinical picture strongly points to laryngomalacia exacerbated by reflux. I am not requesting further tests at this time as the diagnosis is supported by the specific history provided.
